newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** The Cabinet will meet on Friday to take up a host of crucial issues which will include the proposed Tata-Singapore Airlines (Tata-SIA) joint venture, the Business Standard says.

Uplinking for foreign broadcasters from Indian soil and a liberalised coal policy permitting imports and foreign investment in mining are the other issues that are likely to be taken up, the paper reports.
** The head of a German business delegation urged India on Thursday to reduce bureaucratic red tape to help raise an "alarming" level of foreign direct investment.
Hans-Olaf Henkel, president of the Federation of German Industries (BDI), said India lagged far behind China in attracting foreign investment and needed to pull down barriers to private initiative.
Although India's economy was growing, "in comparison to other Asian economies, the shortcomings in foreign direct investment are alarming," he told the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).
** Indians used to religious riots may see energy riots as the nation's power shortage was assuming alarming proportions, a top civil servant warned on Thursday.
"You may see riots -- not in the communal sense, but for lack of power," P.Abraham, secretary of the federal ministry of power told reporters after addressing a business conference.
India had a 10 percent energy shortage (20 percent peak hour shortage) equivalent to about 10,000 MW a year, Abraham said.

He said the government would soon introduce laws to amend the electricity act and set up independent regulatory commissions to fix tariffs to ensure a minimum of three percent return to utility companies.

** Swiss electrical giant Asea Brown Boveri and Siemens AG of Germany have decided to approach the government for permission to set up two steam-based power plants in the country, the Business Line newspaper reports.

The power plants would be set up within a time span of 48 months on a turnkey basis. On being permitted, the multinationals would take the independent power producers' route and look for a partner to set up the project, the paper says.

** The impressive performance of both the manufacturing and the services sectors helped push up the overall gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate to 7.1 percent during 1995/96 (April-March), the Observer says.
This was against 7.2 percent GDP growth rate in the
previous year, the paper says.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened unchanged at 35.85/86 against the dollar on Friday and was expected to hold at this level, dealers said.
** Indian bourses resume trading after a national holiday on Thursday. The top 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange .BSESN on Wednesday rose 44.35 points, or 1.31 percent to end at 3,427.09.
